plan: Given the private value of $10, bid below this to ensure profit if winning. The worst-case scenario is winning and paying a bid equal to my value, resulting in zero profit. To minimize risk, bid slightly below $10. This balances the chance of winning with potential profit. Since this is the only round, prioritize immediate profit.

Evaluate the worst-case scenario for each bid. If I bid $30, I win if others bid less. The worst case is paying $0 and gaining $30. If I bid higher, I risk paying more than the value. If I bid lower, I risk losing the item. Thus, bidding $30 maximizes profit while ensuring I don't overpay in the worst case.

Given my value of $25, I'll bid slightly below it to ensure a positive expected profit while minimizing losses. The worst-case scenario is winning with a bid near my value and paying close to it, resulting in little to no profit. I'll bid $24 to maximize chances of winning without overpaying. This balances risk and reward, ensuring a positive outcome even in the worst case.
